extracted.intended_audience: journalists, newsroom editors, standards editors, and journalism students
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative criteria and questions for contemporary journalism ethics and newsroom standards, focusing on how to cover false information, use AI, protect sources, maintain objectivity, and preserve editorial independence and public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covering false information / calling out lies
rubrics_metrics.description: How Should Journalists Call Out Lies in the Age of Trump and AI? — Journalists must find new ways to talk about false information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Politicians lie to the media and to the public, and we have to decide how to cover those lies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI tools and meeting journalistic standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Can AI Tools Meet Journalistic Standards? — So far, the results are spotty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rapid growth of AI presents new quandaries; as digital tools advance, there are more ways than ever to seek the truth and more ways to lose trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectivity in reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Is Objectivity Still Worth Pursuing? — A generation of journalists is challenging traditional standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internally, journalists are debating the merits of objectivity in the approach to news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities to sources and audiences / source protection
rubrics_metrics.description: What Do Journalists Owe Their Sources—and Their Audiences? — As digital tools advance, there are more ways than ever to seek the truth. There are also more ways to lose trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists must consider how to best protect their sources while fulfilling obligations to audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical funding and protecting editorial independence
rubrics_metrics.description: For Nonprofit Newsrooms, Ethical Funding Is Essential — How outlets are updating their strategies to protect editorial independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rise of nonprofit newsrooms brings new questions about funding and how funding models affect newsroom independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamining newsroom ethics in a changing landscape
rubrics_metrics.description: Thirteen Journalists on How They Are Rethinking Ethics — We asked newsroom leaders and ethicists what they’re keeping or changing in an era of Trump, 'fake news,' AI, and industry decline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collective reflection across newsrooms on which long-standing ethical practices should be retained or revised given current political and technological pressures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updating journalistic ethics for contemporary challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Times Change, and So Can Ethics — Journalism needs new guidelines to face new challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A call to modernize standards and practices in light of declining trust, political misinformation, technological change, and industry transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building and preserving public trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust in the press has declined; journalists must consider how ethical choices affect public confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions about calling out falsehoods, objectivity, source protection, AI usage, and funding transparency should be evaluated by their impact on maintaining or restoring trust.
